content:
If you're like me, you've probably spent plenty of time on Wikipedia, clicking around reading all sorts of random articles. Now there's finally an official app—wait, no, it should be a widget—for you to do exactly that.

Finally, there's a button that can directly open a random Wikipedia article.

Today's Wikipedia iOS app update adds an interesting and practical new feature: a "Random Article" widget that can be placed on the home screen of your iPhone and iPad.

It comes in two sizes (large and medium), and even has a cute mascot.

Tapping the widget will take you to a completely random Wikipedia article and enable Random mode for you.

No need to leave the app and tap the widget again—just tap the random button, and it'll roll the dice, taking you deeper and deeper into this random maze.

Have fun, but be careful not to lose track of time! Earlier this summer, the Wikipedia app also added a history trivia mini-game.

After you update the Wikipedia iPhone and iPad app today, you can find this new widget.

Make the most of your Apple devices
